utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: Morning, everyone. Monday the twenty-eighth. Can you all hear me, or am I talking to myself again?

utterances.speaker: Hannah Price
utterances.text: We can hear you. I'm more concerned about the broken coffee machine in the canteen. That's a grim start.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: That coffee was grim when it worked, to be fair.

utterances.speaker: Hannah Price
utterances.text: Yeah, and the heating in the portakabin's either tropical or off. Just having a moan, before that goes on your action list.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: There's a birthday cake in the office, if that improves things. No idea whose birthday, but it's there.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: Good enough provenance for me.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: Right, before we all disappear for cake, what's already cleared?

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: I finished the repair on the line 3 barrel last night. That's done, not carrying anything over on that.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: Lovely. Keeping that in the completed bit, then.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: And we were going to replace the belt on the line three but that's been pushed to next month so ignore it. Not happening today.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Yeah, that's off today's schedule. The old entry isn't another job.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: While we're on completed stuff, I already swapped the filter on the hot bearing yesterday.

utterances.speaker: Grace Liu
utterances.text: Right, filter swap's finished. Useful to keep that separate from the bearing work.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: I noticed the pop valve was running a bit warm on nights but it settled down. Just an observation, nothing I'm allocating off that.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: Yeah, understood. Settled down, rather than an ongoing fault.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: The other thing is we can't get to the HV board until production gives us a window. Still blocked.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: Understood. It stays blocked; we're not giving anyone that work in this meeting.

utterances.speaker: Priya Raman
utterances.text: And the supplier still hasn't confirmed the delivery for the hot bearing. Same position as before, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: That's the incoming replacement, yeah? Not saying we can't do anything on what's installed.

utterances.speaker: Priya Raman
utterances.text: Yeah, exactly. Delivery's the blocker. I'm not announcing a replacement job.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: PR, can you do the lock-out tag-out sign-off on the door switch on two this morning? That one's safety critical, straight away.

utterances.speaker: Priya Raman
utterances.text: Yep, I'll do the lock-out tag-out sign-off on the door switch on two straight away this morning.

utterances.speaker: Grace Liu
utterances.text: Yeah, the sign-off, not just somebody saying the switch looks all right.

utterances.speaker: Priya Raman
utterances.text: Absolutely. Proper isolation sign-off is what I'm accepting.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: Haley, can you recalibrate the sensors on the little water valve on two? Top priority please.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll recalibrate the sensors on the little water valve on two. Got it as top priority.

utterances.speaker: Priya Raman
utterances.text: Sorry, talking over you there—sensors, rather than changing anything on the valve itself?

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: That's it, calibration on the sensors. Not a valve replacement.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: Fiona, can you take vibration readings on the turbine two next week? It's urgent.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Me taking the readings, rather than just putting someone else in the planner?

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: Yes, you taking them, please. Next week is the timing, but it's urgent, not a spare-time one.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Right, understood. I'll take vibration readings on the turbine two next week and keep it marked urgent.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Easy to lose that distinction when everything on the sheet says 'arrange', isn't it.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Exactly. Otherwise I come away thinking I've only got a scheduling job.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: Whitty, can you update the risk assessment for work on the hot bearing for Monday? It's urgent.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Monday as in today, yeah? Just making sure I'm not mentally sticking it a week out.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: Yeah, Monday, today. It's urgent.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Okay, I'll update the risk assessment for work on the hot bearing for Monday. Understood on the urgency.

utterances.speaker: Grace Liu
utterances.text: And I'll grease and check the bearings on the hot bearing at half two. Not an emergency but don't let it slip—that's how I've got that one.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: Thanks, Grace. Agreed, at half two, and that priority's right: not an emergency but don't let it slip.

utterances.speaker: Grace Liu
utterances.text: Yep. Grease and bearing checks, separate from the filter that's already been swapped.

utterances.speaker: Hannah Price
utterances.text: I'll organise the toolbox talk for the team at half two as well. That's a whenever you get a chance one, rather than something to drop everything for.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: Cheers, Han. At half two for organising that, then. Yeah, whenever you get a chance in terms of priority.

utterances.speaker: Hannah Price
utterances.text: Yep, that's what I mean. I'll organise it; I'm not trying to pull everyone off the floor right now.

utterances.speaker: Grace Liu
utterances.text: I heard half two twice and thought I'd volunteered to be in two places. Different jobs, different people. Fine.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: Yeah, no double booking hidden in that.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: Fiona Doyle, can you run the monthly fire alarm test as well? Fairly important, that one.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Yes, I'll run the monthly fire alarm test. Got that as fairly important.

utterances.speaker: Hannah Price
utterances.text: That's separate from my toolbox talk, just so nobody's bundled them together.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: Yep, two separate things. Not making the talk into an alarm test.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: And I'll send the shift handover report round next Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: Thanks, Doyler. Shift handover report round next Tuesday, agreed.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Yep, next Tuesday. That's the report circulation, not another bit of work on the equipment.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: I'll check the guarding on the palletiser as well. Not an emergency but don't let it slip.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: Cheers, Marc. Guarding on the palletiser is yours, with that priority.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: Yep, I'll do the guarding check. That's what I'm taking on.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Not the belt job sneaking back onto the list under a different name, then.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: No, definitely not. The belt on the line three is still pushed to next month. Different thing entirely.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: Right. And the HV board access and the unconfirmed delivery stay as blockers, not fresh actions we've handed out.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Correct. Neither's suddenly become available because we've talked about it.

utterances.speaker: Priya Raman
utterances.text: If only Teams worked like that. Half our problems would disappear on mute.

utterances.speaker: Hannah Price
utterances.text: Unlike the coffee machine. Still broken when I unmute. Cake might have to do.

utterances.speaker: Callum Reid
utterances.text: Right, that's the lot. Thanks, all. Clear enough despite us talking over each other.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: Yeah, all clear. Cheers.
